newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end slightly up on big-caps.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end slightly up on big-caps.

text.p: Jakarta share prices closed slightly up on Friday due to bargain-hunting in some blue chips, brokers said.
Major issues such as cigarette maker Sampoerna, telecommunications firm Telkom Indonesia, noodle maker Indofood and Citra Marga were among the favourites of bargain-hunters, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index rose 0.70 points, or 0.10 percent, to close at 683.81 points after rising to 684.70 points earlier. However, in the broader market, losers led gainers by 68 to 54, with 58 counters unchanged.
Compared to last Friday's close of 705.37 points, the index was down 3.1 percent, or 21.56 points, on the week.

"Concern over the possibility of a possible hike in U.S interest rates after (Federal Reserve chairman Alan) Greenspan's comments ... underlined the weak tone in the market," Fadjar Sutandi, head of research at Sigma Batara brokerage, said.

"There should be some correction after recent sharp rises, but fundamentally, there is no negative news on Indonesia," he added. Fadjar said U.S employment figures which would be announced on Friday could give some direction to the market in the coming week.
"Some company listings are likely to boost market activity in the next week," he added.
Local-led active buying in several medium stocks also helped the index inch up, brokers said.
Holding company Bakrie & Brothers was the most active stock with some 17 million shares traded at an unchanged price of 1,175 rupiah.

Brokers said it was linked to news that it estimated its 1996 net profit at 193 billion rupiah against 120 billion rupiah in 1995. Investors were also enthused by news that Bakrie is mulling the possibility of listing its infrastructure, chemical and telecommunications units in 1998.
Retailer Multipolar, a unit of the Lippo Group, was also active, with some 16.9 million shares changing hands.

It closed 75 rupiah higher at 3,275 rupiah on talk the founder of retailer Matahari, Hari Darmawan, had begun to buy shares of Multipolar from the market. News reports had said he planned to take a 20-percent stake in the firm.
Banking stocks Bank Negara Indonesia and Bank International Indonesia were targets of sellers, brokers said.

Bank PDFCI topped the gainers list, rising about 20 percent, to 2,800 rupiah on a volume of some five million shares on what brokers said was partly due to speculation the bank had been targeted for a takeover by a conglomerate.
A Bank PDFCI official said all of the company's corporate activities had been made known to the public.
